notes: It works and its end-to-end tests are good, but the design is convoluted: NewObject and New compare computed remotes and retry with trimmed suffixes instead of naming entries consistently, and zip Open gains symlink-only offset hacks that make it inconsistent with regular files.

The code is identical to the reference, but the tests are thinner than its siblings: there is no zip seek/range coverage, no regular .rclonelink member test, and no NewObject-agreement check in the squashfs test.

It is correct and adds precedence handling for a regular `x.rclonelink` colliding with a symlink `x`, plus a shared OpenLink helper, but it is heavier than needed: it decompresses every zip symlink at listing time (costly on remote archives), adds a size cap, and uses a looser Readlink interface assertion.

The code is identical to the reference, and the tests are thorough: seek/range for both backends, NewObject agreement without --links, a regular .rclonelink member, a sub-root mount and the hostile-archive escape, with docs added.

The code matches the reference for both zip and squashfs, and the tests cover skip/translate behaviour, seek/range reads, regular .rclonelink members, NewObject agreement, the squashfs path and hostile-archive escape; the docs addition is appropriate.
